text: A California mail ballot postmarked on Election Day still counts if it arrives up to 7 days later.
seenIn: an Instagram story on Election Day

room.label: students (demo crowd)
room.note: No published poll has measured this belief yet. The 5C pilot survey replaces this split with real student answers.

truthSource.label: California Secretary of State: Vote by Mail
truthSource.oneLine: Mailed ballots must be postmarked on or before Election Day and received no later than 7 days after it. Postmarks can lag, so mail early or use a drop box.

lesson.tip: Many states require ballots to arrive by Election Day, so national posts often get California wrong in either direction. Deadlines are state law: check your own state’s election office.
